html:
SMTO-EXE-0095 — SMTO couldn't read text from this image

GUID: 991c15de-0cf5-5874-b930-a631852294e8
Slug: screen-ocr-input
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: screen

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use the image or settings it was given for reading text, or the text-reading program sent back results that didn't make sense. No text was returned.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you pointed SMTO at an image file, give the full path to a PNG or JPEG saved on the Gateway's own computer. SMTO refuses web links, network folders, shortcuts and partial paths for safety.
  2. Open the image yourself to check it isn't damaged, and save it again as PNG or JPEG if it won't open or is another type. A damaged or mislabeled picture can't be read.
  3. If you asked for a searchable PDF, use a resolution (DPI) between 72 and 300. SMTO refuses resolutions outside that range for searchable PDFs.
  4. If the text is on screen, ask SMTO to read it straight from the screen instead of from a file. Reading from the screen skips the file checks entirely.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns the text it read from the image.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send it, with the image's file name and type, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste the image or its contents into the report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OCR input or output validation failed: unsafe or unsupported local image path, undecodable raster, DPI outside 72-300, failed Tesseract output, malformed word data, or word boxes outside the source rectangle.

What this means

  • OCR input/output validation rejected an unsafe local image path, malformed raster, invalid DPI, failed provider output, malformed word data or word coordinates outside the source rectangle. Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.

Why this can happen

  • OCR input/output validation rejected an unsafe local image path, malformed raster, invalid DPI, failed provider output, malformed word data or word coordinates outside the source rectangle.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the failed check concerns path/image preparation, DPI, provider processing or parsed output geometry.

How to fix it

  • ScreenService._local_image needs an absolute path to a regular local PNG/JPEG on the selected Gateway (no '..', UNC or network paths, links or URLs); searchable_pdf needs integer DPI 72-300 and real PDF output; Tesseract TSV must parse and every word box must lie inside the source rectangle. Inspect the Tesseract exit status and output before replacing the input.
  • Correct the specific path, image, DPI or output-validation problem. Use a supported local source or explicit screen target; inspect provider failures before replacing input unnecessarily.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use an existing regular local PNG/JPEG on the selected Gateway or an explicit screen target. URLs, network paths, links and malformed images are rejected.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported local source and valid settings yield bounded words with coordinates inside the observed image.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass OS permissions, capture another Gateway, or copy screen content to diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • Screen and OCR observations occur only through their existing explicit request and permission flow. Rendering diagnostics neither captures pixels nor reads additional content, and no failed observation is silently repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
